stated: The Conservative Party will restore public trust in policing by licensing officers for specialist roles, legislating for appropriate vetting during service, and ensuring officers who fail can be sacked.

source.quote: Restore public trust in policing. We will license police officers for specialist roles, as we do already for firearms officers. We will legislate to ensure officers are appropriately vetted during their service and those who fail can be sacked.

bearing_set.reason: Directly targets police vetting, licensing, and dismissal powers — measures that bear on policing quality, accountability, and public safety outcomes.

Improved vetting and the power to remove officers who fail bears directly on equal treatment and minority protections: inadequately vetted officers have been a documented source of discriminatory conduct and due-process failures.
The policy's explicit goal is to 'restore public trust in policing'; institutional trust in police is a measurable component of social trust and community cohesion, which are core O15 indicators.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: a safety/justice quality effect (O5), an equal-treatment/minority-protection effect (O9), and a social-trust effect (O15). No plausible non-negligible worsening of other fundamentals clears the mechanistic bar — the fiscal cost of an administrative vetting system is too small to materially affect O12, and the policy does not expand coercive powers over citizens so O10 is not triggered.
